title: Return type alone cannot overload a method
answer: Changing only the return type does not create a valid overload because Java method signatures for overload resolution do not include the return type. Two methods with the same name and identical parameter types therefore conflict even if one returns `int` and the other returns `String`. AeroTopo's `CompilerRulesTest` includes exactly this illegal declaration and requires the compiler to report an error.
